title: Claude beyond code · 3 non-coding ways I use Claude (carousel 1167)
summary: Metricool: scheduled Mon 12 Oct 13:00 IG + IG trial reel + TikTok. 3 ways I use Claude that aren't coding.
body: Metricool: scheduled Mon 12 Oct 13:00 IG + IG trial reel + TikTok. 3 ways I use Claude that aren't coding.
guide: This shows three everyday, non-coding jobs you can give Claude, such as writing, planning and sorting information. You need a Claude account (claude.ai) and a few real tasks of your own.
1. Pick three jobs from your week that involve words or information rather than code, such as replying to emails, planning a project or summarising a long document.
1. Open Claude at claude.ai and start a new Project for each job so it keeps its own instructions and files.
1. Add context to each Project: upload a few examples of your own work and write a short note on tone and audience.
1. Paste in the real task and ask Claude for a first draft or plan.
1. Reply with specific corrections ("shorter", "less formal", "add the deadline") rather than starting again.
1. Save the version you like as a reusable instruction in the Project so the next run starts from it.
1. Check the result against the source before you send or publish it.
Watch out: Claude can sound confident when it is wrong, so read every figure, name and date yourself before using the output.

```
You are helping me set up Claude for non-coding work. My role is <your role>. I want to use Claude for three jobs: <job 1>, <job 2> and <job 3>. I have access to <Claude plan, for example the free tier or Pro> and I can upload <file types I have, for example Word documents, PDFs or notes>.
For each job, do the following:
1. Write a short set of Project instructions I can paste into Claude, covering tone, audience, length and anything it must never do.
2. List which example files or notes I should upload so Claude learns my style.
3. Give me one starter prompt I can use on a real task straight away.
4. Give me a short checklist for reviewing the output before I use it.
Keep everything in plain English, with no jargon. Use British spelling. Do not invent facts about my business; if you need information, ask me first. Return the three jobs as separate sections, each with the four items above in order.
```
